2609.30897.title: From annotation to reasoning: Culture in language models
2609.30897.paper_summary: How should we evaluate language models when more than one interpretation can be right? Cultural benchmarks often test factual knowledge, agreement with survey responses, or recognition of a predefined meaning. These tasks leave open whether a model can explain how a cultural reference works in a particular text, support a reading with evidence, or revise it after criticism. This is a question of interpretive depth, complementary to the breadth of cultural coverage. We argue that literary interpretation offers a useful setting for studying these capabilities. We focus on cultural referencing and reuse: how texts invoke, repeat, and transform earlier expressions across historical and linguistic contexts. Our central claim is that literary scholars can disagree about an interpretation while recognizing the quality of its support. We propose linking evidence-centered benchmarks, evaluation that preserves scholarly disagreement, and model-development experiments on literary data, contextual resources, and scholarly feedback. Danish literature provides a concrete starting point, with implications for other languages and domains. The aim is to develop alternative evaluation strategies that go beyond conventional benchmark metrics and guide model development toward cultural robustness in AI systems.
2609.30897.paper_summary_zh: 如何評估語言模型，當多種解釋都可能是正確的時候？文化基準通常測試事實知識、與調查回應的一致性，或對預定義意義的識別。這些任務未考慮模型是否能解釋文化參考在特定文本中的運作方式、是否能用證據支持某種解讀，或在批評後進行修訂。這是一個解釋深度的問題，與文化涵蓋的廣度互補。我們認為文學解釋提供了一個有用的背景來研究這些能力。我們專注於文化參考和重用：文本如何在歷史和語言背景中喚起、重複和轉化早期表達。我們的核心主張是，文學學者可以對某一解釋持不同意見，同時承認其支持的質量。我們建議將以證據為中心的基準、保留學術分歧的評估，以及基於文學數據、上下文資源和學術反饋的模型開發實驗聯繫起來。丹麥文學提供了一個具體的起點，對其他語言和領域具有啟示。目標是開發超越傳統基準指標的替代評估策略，並指導模型開發朝向AI系統的文化穩健性。
